Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

betaMC 1.3.5

Minor

  • New FSqMC(): Cohen’s f-squared and the local f-squared of each regressor.
  • New SCorSqMC(): the image of a signed-semipartial interval under squaring.
  • Faster Monte Carlo: the draws are screened and the effect sizes computed in C++ (Rcpp, RcppArmadillo), once per MC() or MCMI() call. The draws are the same as before for the same seed.
  • The thetahatstar elements of mc and betamc objects are now matrices (one draw per row) instead of lists. mc objects also hold vechsigmacap and es.
  • A draw that fails the admissibility checks 1000 times in a row is dropped (earlier versions could loop without end).
  • Selective standardization: the arguments std_y and std_x standardize only y or only the named regressors (for example, leave a dummy variable in its 0-1 units). The defaults give the same results as before.
  • The internal copies from linearAlgebra 0.0.5 (a faster duplication matrix and its inverse), nBootstrap 0.1.0 (quantiles in C++), strRegression 0.0.2, and processLM 0.0.11 are current. The pseudo-inverse of the duplication matrix is now exact, so results for a fixed seed may differ slightly from 1.3.4; the difference is within Monte Carlo error.

Patch

  • MC() and MCMI() stop with an error for an lm fit without an intercept, with weights, or with an offset. These fits were accepted before, and the results were wrong.
  • DiffBetaMC() computes the differences of the standardized slopes without a loop.
  • Documentation: the MC() and MCMI() help pages list FSqMC() and SCorSqMC() among the functions that accept their output; SCorSqMC() joins the Beta Monte Carlo family.
  • Documentation: formulas use \operatorname{} and \boldsymbol{}; the undefined \matnrm{} macro in the Monte Carlo bias, variance, and RMSE help pages is now \mathrm{}; the DOI links use https.

Documentation

  • The examples name every argument and call stats::lm().
  • DeltaRSqMC() cites Algina, Keselman, and Penfield (2007, 2008a, 2008b, 2010), as DeltaRSqSandwich() and DeltaRSqNB() do.

betaMC 1.3.0

CRAN release: 2023-08-22

Minor

  • Added the MCMI() function to perform Monte Carlo simulation of parameters for data sets with missing values using multiple imputation.

betaMC 1.2.0

CRAN release: 2023-04-13

Minor

  • The Monte Carlo simulation of parameters is done by the MC() function. The output of the MC() function is passed to the BetaMC(), RSqMC(), SCorMC(), DeltaRSqMC(), PCorMC(), and DiffBetaMC() functions to generate Monte Carlo confidence intervals for various regression effect sizes.
